Discovery ran over the south batch and wrote both files to the working folder. It emitted 10 candidates, all marked proposed and advisory (deontic). Nothing was applied to the model.

- Proposal: `<workspace>/south-discovery.proposal.json`
- Report: `<workspace>/south-discovery.report.md`

The proposal is recorded as actor `reader` at `2026-10-26T00:00:00Z`, as you asked. That date is a month before today's date (2026-11-25); I used it as given.

**Reading the rules back.** In GND, a uniqueness rule on one role means "at most one", and a mandatory rule means "at least one". "Exactly one" is the two together.

**"Each X has exactly one Y"**
1. **Each refund has exactly one amount.** Half is proposed (each refund has at most one amount) and half is proposed (each refund has at least one amount). Sensible.
2. **Each refund has exactly one channel.** Half is proposed (each refund is paid by at most one channel) and half is proposed (each refund is paid by at least one channel). Sensible.
3. **Each refund has exactly one customer.** The "at most one" half is already declared in the model. The new suggestion is the "at least one" half: every refund has a customer. Sensible.

**"Every X has a Y"** (these are the "at least one" halves of the rules above, plus three more)
- Every refund has a customer, an amount and a channel. Sensible; these are the halves in rules 1–3.
- **Every customer has a refund.** Doubtful. It is an accident of one store's week, not a business rule.
- **Every amount has a refund.** Doubtful. It treats amounts as if each had to belong to a refund.
- **Every channel has a refund.** Doubtful. It says each payment channel must appear this week. A week with no voucher refunds would break it.

**Other suggestions (at most one, not in the two kinds you asked for)**
- **Each customer has at most one refund** this week. Doubtful; a sample accident.
- **Each amount belongs to at most one refund.** Doubtful; two refunds of the same amount are normal.

My read: the five refund-level rules are the sensible ones (rules 1–3 and their halves). The other five are artifacts of three refunds in one store's week, and I'd expect you to drop them when you review. The report also shows one candidate was rejected by the checker with a warning; it does not say which.

None of the candidates carries host values, since no value-family candidates were emitted.

**Next step:** the proposal goes to review in gnd-model-evolve, which previews it and applies only what you accept. Tell me which candidates you want kept and I can route only those.

print(list(p.keys()))
